regional_status: Top priority quarantine-level foliar threat in Punjab (sub-mountainous districts: Hoshiarpur, Ropar, Gurdaspur) and Haryana (Ambala, Yamunanagar, Panchkula).
symptoms: Bright yellow to lemon-yellow pustules (urediniospores) arranged in continuous linear stripes or chains along the leaf veins on the upper leaf surface. A yellow powdery mass easily rubs off onto fingers or white clothes. Severely infected leaves dry out, turn brown, and curl upwards.
favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (10°C to 15°C) with persistent cloud cover, rain showers, and heavy morning dew during January and February.
prevention_practices: Grow yellow rust-resistant wheat varieties approved by PAU/IIWBR (e.g., PBW 824, PBW 826, HD 3226, DBW 222, DBW 187).
Avoid planting susceptible legacy cultivars (e.g., HD 2967, PBW 343) in vulnerable sub-mountainous belts.
Scout lower leaves of crops weekly from late December onwards, particularly near tree shades and canal banks.
management_practices: Upon noticing initial yellow pustule stripes on isolated patches, spray Propiconazole 25 EC (0.1%) or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC immediately.
Dissolve fungicide in 200 liters of water per acre using a flat-fan nozzle for uniform canopy coverage.
Repeat spray after 15 days if cool, wet conditions persist and fresh yellow pustules reappear.
Notify local PAU/HAU agricultural officer or KVK upon first detection.
safety_warning: Wear protective clothing, goggles, and gloves. Do not spray during windy conditions to avoid drift onto non-target crops or livestock fodder.

regional_status: Widespread across all agro-climatic zones of Punjab and Haryana during warm spring days of late February and March.
symptoms: Round to oval, reddish-orange to bright orange-brown pustules scattered randomly across the upper leaf surface (not arranged in linear rows like yellow rust). As leaves mature, black telia appear as dark brown or black crusts.
favorable_conditions: Warmer temperatures (15°C to 25°C) with free moisture on leaves (heavy dew or spring rain).
prevention_practices: Sow timely in November to ensure grain filling completes before high temperature rust pressure rises in March.
Sow certified rust-resistant varieties recommended by IIWBR Karnal (e.g., HD 3086, PBW 725, DBW 303).
Ensure balanced potassic fertilizer application to enhance rust tolerance.
management_practices: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC or Tebuconazole 25.9 EC when pustules appear on flag leaves.
Protect the flag leaf at all costs, as it contributes over 75% of grain filling nutrition.
safety_warning: Observe chemical withholding periods before harvesting. Use dedicated crop sprayer tanks.

regional_status: Infrequent in northern plains due to winter cold, but periodically monitored in late-sown wheat.
symptoms: Elongated, reddish-brown pustules (uredinia) that erupt through the epidermis on stems, leaf sheaths, leaves, and glumes, producing prominent jagged ragged epidermal fringes around each pustule. Pustules turn coal-black (telia) as crop matures.
favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (above 20°C to 30°C) with moist vegetation.
management_practices: Apply protective foliar triazole fungicides (Propiconazole 25 EC) if stem lesions are verified by agricultural extension.

regional_status: Common in shaded field pockets, dense lodging canopies, and sub-mountainous zones of Punjab.
symptoms: White to grayish powdery fluffy patches on leaf blades and sheaths. As infection ages, the powdery patches turn dull brownish-gray and develop minute black specks (cleistothecia). Underlying leaf tissue turns yellow and prematurely senesces.
favorable_conditions: High humidity (85% to 100%), cool temperatures (15°C to 20°C), and dense over-fertilized crop canopies.
prevention_practices: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces lush, succulent, vulnerable foliage.
Maintain recommended seed rates (40 kg/acre) to avoid overly dense tillering.
management_practices: Spray Propiconazole 25 EC or Wettable Sulphur 80 WP at disease inception in dense canopies.
Ensure spray reaches into the lower canopy layer.
safety_warning: Do not spray sulphur during high afternoon temperatures (>30°C) to prevent foliar scorch.

regional_status: Normal robust growth stage in timely sown wheat.
symptoms: Upright, uniform, dark-green canopy; absence of chlorotic stripes, yellow/orange pustules, or powdery efflorescence.
favorable_conditions: Well-tilled loamy soil, adequate basal phosphorus (DAP/SSP), optimal crown root initiation (CRI) irrigation.
prevention_practices: Apply first irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage (21 days after sowing).
Apply zinc sulphate if soil test indicates deficiency to prevent chlorotic striping.
management_practices: Follow PAU/HAU recommended schedule for timely weed management and split nitrogen top-dressing.
safety_warning: Ensure clean water usage and safe handling of farm machinery.
